analysis.title: Paul Donovan's daily audio: Tit for tat, in war and trade
key_insights: UK October CPI came in line with expectations. Fuel costs were the main driver of the increase.
UK output producer price inflation was slightly lower than expected. The report says this is not likely to move investors.
Iran reported strikes on US military bases in Kuwait and Bahrain. UBS describes a relatively low-level tit-for-tat exchange of attacks between the US and Iran.
UBS says the US-Iran exchange is not sufficient to dent the oil market's optimism bias.
China's President Xi warned against escalating trade tensions ahead of a scheduled meeting with US President Trump.
China expressed anger at proposed US chip export bans and threatened retaliation. The most disruptive option might be limiting China's rare earth exports.
US importers have become adept at avoiding tariffs by disguising imports from China.
European politicians appear to have concluded negotiations over ECB jobs. Spain's de Cos looks set to become ECB president. UBS says policy is unlikely to change but communication style may.

macro_indicators.interpretation: Fuel costs were the main cause of the increase. The report says the data was dull and not market-moving.
The report says it is not going to motivate investors.

risk_factors: Escalation of the US-Iran military exchange.
China retaliation over US chip export bans, including rare earth export limits.
geopolitical: Iran reported strikes on US military bases in Kuwait and Bahrain, part of what the report calls the Gulf War.
